name: Melanoma
theme: the immunotherapy flagship · the neoadjuvant turn

meta.title: Melanoma in silico decision trainer
meta.population: Adults with cutaneous melanoma - the registry's immunotherapy flagship, where a decade of checkpoint blockade produced the number the whole field is measured by (CheckMate 067 at ten years: median overall survival 71.9 months with nivolumab + ipilimumab, and median melanoma-specific survival still not reached beyond 120 months) and where the newest chapter is the NEOADJUVANT TURN: giving the immunotherapy BEFORE surgery, with the tumor still in place as the antigen source, beat the same drugs given after (S1801; NADINA EFS HR 0.32) - so decisively that the 2026 guideline made neoadjuvant the preferred initial approach for resectable nodal disease. Uveal and mucosal melanoma are different biology (tebentafusp's HLA-restricted door belongs to uveal; low-TMB KIT biology to mucosal) and reroute. This spec was authored on a day the field moved twice: the INTerpath-001 individualized-neoantigen phase 3 announced positive topline the morning of the sweep, and the RP1 oncolytic's accelerated approval was thirteen days old.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the disease that taught oncology immunotherapy. The metastatic flagship ranks on the field's deepest receipt: CheckMate 067's final ten-year analysis (median OS 71.9 months with nivo+ipi; median melanoma-specific survival not reached at more than 120 months, with 37% alive at trial end; and among patients alive and progression-free at three years, 10-year melanoma-specific survival 96% - a functional-cure tail rendered honestly). DREAMseq settles the BRAF-mutant sequencing question (IO-first 2-yr OS 71.8% vs 51.5% targeted-first), so the targeted card…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: AJCC 8th edition (Breslow thickness + ulceration drive T; sentinel node drives III) - v9 status unconfirmed, flagged; BRAF testing universal in stage III/IV; NCCN risk framework secondhand (403)
meta.response: RECIST 1.1 for metastatic disease; for the neoadjuvant era the load-bearing read is PATHOLOGIC RESPONSE at surgery - NADINA's major pathologic response (59%) drives response-adapted de-escalation, making the pathology report itself the treatment-duration decision

Newly diagnosed.name: Wide excision (thin disease - surgery cures nearly all)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: surgical standard (framing); survival figure flagged (SEER secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: a scar and a calendar - the lightest curative card in this trainer
Newly diagnosed.patient: For thin melanoma: an outpatient operation removes it with a safety margin and cures nearly everyone - the follow-up skin checks are the real long-term plan.

Newly diagnosed.name: Wide excision + staging (IIB/IIC - the curative anchor)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the operation, then the decision about a year of adjuvant immunotherapy - the next card's honest conversation
Newly diagnosed.patient: For thick or ulcerated melanomas that have not reached the nodes: surgery remains the cure for most - with a genuine follow-on conversation about a year of preventive immunotherapy.

Newly diagnosed.name: Adjuvant PD-1 for IIB/IIC (KEYNOTE-716 / CheckMate 76K - the RFS-only honesty)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: FDA-approved adjuvant options for IIB/IIC (dates secondhand); the RFS-only basis said plainly
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized x2 - RFS met in both; OS not shown (labeled, never ranked)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: a year of the immune ledger for a preventive indication - the permanent-endocrinopathy risk weighs differently when the patient is currently cancer-free
Newly diagnosed.patient: A year of preventive immunotherapy after surgery cuts the chance of relapse meaningfully - what it has not yet shown is longer life, and this card says that out loud because the side-effect tab is real.

Newly diagnosed.name: Neoadjuvant ipilimumab + nivolumab (NADINA - the turn itself)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN v2.2026: neoadjuvant PREFERRED for resectable nodal disease, ipi+nivo Category 1 (secondhand); no dedicated FDA neoadjuvant approval -…
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized (NEJM 2024) - EFS decisive; OS unwritten (labeled, never ranked - the unranked menu's centerpiece)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the doublet's immune ledger compressed into the preoperative window - with the 59% chance the pathology report cancels most of the rest
Newly diagnosed.patient: The new preferred road for node-positive melanoma: immunotherapy BEFORE surgery, while the tumor is still there to teach the immune system - it cut relapse events by two-thirds versus the old order, and a deep response at surgery means most of the remaining treatment gets cancelled.

Newly diagnosed.name: Neoadjuvant-adjuvant pembrolizumab (S1801 - the same drug, resequenced)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: PDQ carries the neoadjuvant pembrolizumab section (loaded live); NCCN placement secondhand
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized (S1801, NEJM 2023) - EFS met; OS unwritten (labeled)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: single-agent PD-1 ledger - the gentler neoadjuvant when the doublet's 55.0% grade 3-4 price is the wrong trade
Newly diagnosed.patient: The same immunotherapy drug, given partly before surgery instead of all after - that single change of order cut relapse events dramatically. The gentler one-drug version of the new road.

Newly diagnosed.name: Adjuvant-only pathway (KEYNOTE-054 / COMBI-AD - the era the turn displaced)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: the previous standard - still guideline-listed where neoadjuvant does not fit (secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized x3 - RFS met in all; OS unwritten across the era (labeled)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: a year of adjuvant therapy by choice of agent - the immune ledger or the targeted one (pyrexia leads COMBI-AD's)
Newly diagnosed.patient: The until-recently-standard order: surgery first, then a year of preventive therapy - still real and still right for some, now honestly second to the immunotherapy-first road for most node-positive disease.

Newly diagnosed.name: Nivolumab + ipilimumab (CheckMate 067 - the ten-year flagship)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: the 1L standard for fit stage IV (NCCN secondhand); ten-year evidence
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized, TEN-YEAR maturity (NEJM 2025) - the flagship
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the hardest immune season in oncology (55.0% grade 3-4 in the primary report, colitis/hepatitis/endocrine) - bought against a coin-flip chance of decades; perm…
Newly diagnosed.patient: The strongest treatment melanoma has: two immune drugs together gave half of patients survival past ten years in the landmark trial - through an intense first season of side effects that a good team manages hard.
drugs: Nivolumab + ipilimumab (relatlimab+nivo as the gentler doublet note)

Newly diagnosed.name: Nivolumab monotherapy (the gentler road, measured in the same trial)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized, ten-year maturity (same trial as the flagship)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the single-agent immune ledger (24% grade 3-4) - the denominator the doublet's price is measured against
Newly diagnosed.patient: The single immune drug: real long-term survival (four in ten alive at ten years) with far fewer hard side effects - the honest alternative when the combination's storm is the wrong trade.

Newly diagnosed.name: BRAF/MEK targeted therapy (COMBI-d/v - in the DREAMseq-assigned position)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: BRAF-mutant option - DREAMseq-sequenced to second position for most (NCCN secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 pooled five-year (COMBI-d/v) + randomized sequencing verdict (DREAMseq)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: pyrexia leads the doublet's ledger - a different shape than the immune one, fast on and fast off
Newly diagnosed.patient: For BRAF-mutant melanoma: tablets that work fast and reliably - and a trial that answered the order question directly: immunotherapy first, these tablets second, gives the better long-term survival.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.patient: Declining treatment is a real choice, made with the modern numbers on the table - which in this disease have changed more than in almost any other.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Lifileucel TIL therapy (the first cell therapy for a solid tumor - labeled)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: accelerated approval 2024-02-16 (secondhand) - confirmatory enrolling; the conversion watch is live
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: pooled phase 2 (accelerated); response-grade with an unreached duration tail - labeled
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: the cell-therapy episode: cytopenias from lymphodepletion, IL-2's storm, weeks in specialized care - front-loaded like a transplant
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: When immunotherapy stops working: your own tumor-fighting cells, harvested, multiplied by the billions, and returned - about one in three respond, and responders tend to hold. An intensive hospital episode buys the attempt.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: RP1 + nivolumab (the thirteen-day-old approval - labeled, walk carried)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: accelerated approval 2026-08-06 (fda.gov - the newest approval in melanoma); confirmatory IGNYTE-3 enrolling
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: registrational single-arm ORR (accelerated, post-2-CRL) - labeled; ORR figure flagged pending registry pull
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: injection-site and flu-like effects plus the nivolumab ledger - among the gentler cards on this menu
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The newest option: a modified cold-sore virus injected into a tumor to make it visible to the immune system again, with immunotherapy alongside - approved days before this page was written, on response evidence, with the survival trial enrolling now.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: BRAF/MEK targeted therapy (the post-IO ticket, DREAMseq-sequenced)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: the BRAF+ post-IO standard (NCCN secondhand); DREAMseq's sequence executing
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: For BRAF-mutant disease after immunotherapy: the targeted tablets take their planned turn - quick, dependable shrinkage and a real fraction of long responses.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Choosing comfort after immunotherapy has been tried is a real road - chosen with the true numbers, in the disease where those numbers changed most.

refs.label: Morton et al. MSLT-I final: sentinel-node biopsy - staging value established; MSS benefit in the node-positive intermediate-thickness subgroup. NEJM 2014;370:599-609 (PMID 24521106, verified)

Faries et al. MSLT-II: completion dissection vs observation after positive sentinel node - NO melanoma-specific survival benefit, more lymphedema; ultrasound surveillance replaced the operation. The subtraction. NEJM 2017;376:2211-22 (PMID 28591523, verified)

Luke et al. KEYNOTE-716: adjuvant pembrolizumab for resected IIB/IIC - 36-mo RFS 76.2% vs 63.4% (HR 0.62; final-analysis figures, attribution carried carefully); DMFS also met (PMID 36265502). RFS-ONLY basis said plainly - no OS shown. Lancet 2022 (PMID 35367007, verified)
Kirkwood et al. CheckMate 76K: adjuvant nivolumab for IIB/IIC - RFS HR 0.42, 12-mo RFS 89.0% vs 79.4%. Nat Med 2023 (PMID 37845511, verified)

Eggermont et al. KEYNOTE-054: adjuvant pembrolizumab stage III - 12-mo RFS 75.4% vs 61.0% (HR 0.57; PMID 29658430, verified); 3.5-yr DMFS (PMID 33857412, verified); 5-yr analysis: RFS 55.4% vs 38.3%, DMFS 60.6% vs 44.5% (NEJM Evidence, DOI-verified - PMID deliberately NOT guessed, confirm via registry). No OS readout

Weber et al. CheckMate 238 (5-yr): adjuvant nivolumab vs ipilimumab - 5-yr RFS 50% vs 39% (HR 0.72); grade 3-4 TRAE 14.4% vs 45.9% (the adjuvant-toxicity lesson). Clin Cancer Res 2023 (PMID 37058595, verified; the NEJM 2017 primary PMID not re-confirmed - this is the verified anchor)

Long et al. COMBI-AD: adjuvant dabrafenib+trametinib, resected BRAF-mutant stage III - 3-yr RFS 58% vs 39% (HR 0.47; PMID 28891408); 5-yr RFS 52% vs 36% (HR 0.51; PMID 32877599); final results NEJM 2024 (PMID 38899716) - all verified

Patel et al. SWOG S1801: neoadjuvant-adjuvant vs adjuvant-only pembrolizumab - same drug, same duration, only the ORDER differed: 2-yr EFS 72% vs 49% (p=0.004). The turn's proof-of-principle. NEJM 2023;388:813-23 (PMID 36856617, verified)

Blank et al. NADINA: neoadjuvant ipi+nivo (response-adapted) vs adjuvant nivolumab, resectable stage III - EFS HR 0.32 (99.9% CI 0.15-0.66), 12-mo EFS 83.7% vs 57.2%; MPR 59% -> stop at ~6 weeks. ESMO 2025 update: sustained at 25.2 months (congress-stage). NO OS readout; no dedicated FDA neoadjuvant approval (guideline-driven). NEJM 2024;391:1696-708 (PMID 38828984, verified)

Wolchok et al. CheckMate 067 FINAL TEN-YEAR: median OS 71.9 (nivo+ipi) vs 36.9 (nivo) vs 19.9 months (ipi); median melanoma-specific survival more than 120 months with nivolumab+ipilimumab (not reached, 37% alive at trial end), 49.4 months with nivolumab and 21.9 months with ipilimumab; among patients alive and progression-free at 3 years, 10-year melanoma-specific survival was 96% / 97% / 88% - the functional-cure sentence. NEJM 2025;392(1):11-22 (PMID 39282897), abstract re-read firsthand 2026-09-10. TWO CORRECTIONS made at that read: the previously displayed '10-yr melanoma-specific survival 52%/44%/23%' appears nowhere in the publication and has been removed; and the grade 3-4 treatment-related toxicity belongs to the PRIMARY report, not this one - Larkin et al., N Engl J Med 2015;373(1):23-34 (PMID 26027431, also read firsthand 2026-09-10) gives 55.0% for nivolumab+ipilimumab, 16.3% for nivolumab and 27.3% for ipilimumab, superseding the '59% vs 24%' previously shown

Tawbi et al. RELATIVITY-047: relatlimab + nivolumab vs nivolumab - median PFS 10.1 vs 4.6 months (HR 0.75) - the LAG-3 doublet at near-monotherapy tolerability; PFS-grade, carried as a note (3-yr/4-yr updates exist: PMIDs 39671533/40513285, unopened). NEJM 2022;386:24-34 (PMID 34986285, verified)
Robert et al. Five-year outcomes with dabrafenib+trametinib (COMBI-d/v pooled): 5-yr OS 34%, PFS 19%; complete responders 5-yr OS 71%. NEJM 2019;381:626-36 (PMID 31166680, verified)

Atkins et al. DREAMseq: IO-first (ipi+nivo -> BRAF/MEK) vs targeted-first for BRAF-mutant stage IV - 2-yr OS 71.8% vs 51.5% (p=0.010, stopped early). The sequencing verdict the ranking renders. JCO 2023;41:186-97 (PMID 36166727, verified)

Chesney et al. C-144-01 pooled: lifileucel TIL therapy post-anti-PD-1 - ORR 31.4% (CI 24.1-39.4), median DoR not reached; 5-yr analysis ORR unchanged, CR 5.9% (PMIDs 36600653 + 40454684, verified). FDA ACCELERATED approval 2024-02-16 (first TIL/first solid-tumor cell therapy; secondhand) - NOT converted; TILVANCE-301 confirming. J Immunother Cancer 2022

FDA accelerated approval 2026-08-06: vusolimogene oderparepvec (RP1, oncolytic HSV-1) + nivolumab for advanced cutaneous melanoma progressed on anti-PD-1 - after TWO CRLs (2025-07-22, 2026-04-10) and a 10-3 AdComm vote; based on IGNYTE ORR/DoR (the card's ORR figure flagged pending registry pull). Thirteen days before this spec's authoring - the walk carried verbatim (fda.gov page in search results; direct fetch blocked)

INTerpath-001 (NCT05933577): adjuvant intismeran autogene (V940/mRNA-4157, individualized neoantigen therapy) + pembrolizumab vs pembrolizumab, resected IIB-IV - TOPLINE POSITIVE ANNOUNCED 2026-08-19, THE MORNING OF THIS SWEEP: met RFS primary and DMFS secondary (press release ONLY - no publication, no data, NO approval; phase 2b KEYNOTE-942 basis: 18-mo RFS 79% vs 62%, PMID 38246194 verified + 5-yr JCO 2026 PMID 42223134). Trial ACTIVE NOT RECRUITING - context, not a door. Press-stage discipline: no numbers carried from the topline

Tawbi et al. CheckMate 204 final: nivo+ipi in melanoma brain metastases - intracranial clinical benefit ~57% (CR 26%) in ASYMPTOMATIC patients, durable; sharply lower once symptomatic/steroid-dependent. Lancet Oncol 2021 (PMID 34774225, verified; NEJM 2018 primary not re-confirmed - this is the anchor)

Nathan et al. Tebentafusp in metastatic UVEAL melanoma (the reroute's reason): OS benefit, HLA-A*02:01-restricted gp100xCD3 bispecific - NEJM 2021 (PMID 34551229 - WRONG-PMID CATCH #23: the candidate 34597013 resolved elsewhere; caught on the reroute note itself). 3-yr PMID 37870955; 5-yr PMID 42162665. Zero role in cutaneous disease beyond this note

El-Jawahri A, LeBlanc T, VanDusen H, et al. Effect of Inpatient Palliative Care on Quality of Life 2 Weeks After Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2016;316(20):2094-2103 (PMID 27893130, NCT02207322) — abstract read firsthand 2026-09-10. POPULATION CAUTION, added at that read because the previous label named no population at all: this is a SINGLE-INSTITUTION randomized trial of 160 adults with HAEMATOLOGICAL malignancy hospitalized for autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation, and its outcomes are quality of life, depression, anxiety, fatigue and symptom burden — it reports no survival and no adverse-event table. It is the factory's standing anchor for the PRINCIPLE that palliative care runs alongside active treatment rather than after it; it is not evidence in this tumour type and is not the source of any number on this card.

MSLT-3 (NCT07049276): index-lymph-node resection vs total dissection after 6 weeks neoadjuvant IO, clinical stage IIIB-D, 2-yr RFS non-inferiority (opened 2025-10) - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08, NOT registry-loaded (channel down); US sites likely per MSLT precedent but unconfirmed - re-check due

PRISM-MEL-301 (NCT06112314): brenetafusp (IMC-F106C, PRAME bispecific) + nivolumab vs nivo regimens, 1L advanced melanoma, HLA-A*02:01-POSITIVE required, phase 3, PFS-BICR primary (Immunocore) - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08 (registry cache Feb 2026), NOT registry-loaded - re-check due

TILVANCE-301 (NCT05727904): lifileucel + pembrolizumab vs pembrolizumab, UNTREATED advanced melanoma, ~670 pts, dual ORR/PFS primaries (Iovance) - the accelerated approval's confirmatory - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08, NOT registry-loaded - re-check due

IGNYTE-3 (NCT06264180): RP1 + nivolumab vs physician's choice, advanced melanoma progressed on anti-PD-1 AND anti-CTLA-4 (or CTLA-4-ineligible), injectable lesion required, ~400 pts, OS primary (Replimune) - the thirteen-day-old approval's randomized test - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08 (cache May 2026), NOT registry-loaded - re-check due

SUPRAME (NCT06743126): ACTengine IMA203 (PRAME TCR-T) vs investigator's choice, cutaneous melanoma post-PD-1, HLA-A*02:01-POSITIVE required, phase 3, PFS-BICR primary (Immatics; ~360 pts; 2026 readout projected) - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08, NOT registry-loaded - re-check due

Stanford (NCT06712927): relatlimab + nivolumab + ipilimumab in melanoma brain metastases - ASYMPTOMATIC AND SYMPTOMATIC cohorts (the excluded population enrolled on purpose), phase 2 (opened 2025-08) - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08; PRIMARY ENDPOINT NOT CAPTURED (channel down) - flagged, re-check due.
